subject: Integration gap: request-coalescing errors during FinAI demo
messages:
-----Original Message-----
From: Alan Park <alan@finai.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Demo issue - intermittent 503s at scale during coalescing test

Camila,

Quick note following this morning's live demo with our ML infra team. When we ramped to ~120 r/s and enabled the request-coalescing flag in the SDK the demo started seeing intermittent 503s and a handful of truncated responses. The pattern looks like it happens during burst merges (several clients with similar prefixes).

We captured a short set of logs and a recording — attaching the log bundle separately. Can your team review and advise whether this is a config mismatch or a runtime bug? This is blocking the procurement team from signing.

Thanks,
Alan
Alan Park
Director of Platform Engineering, FinAI
alan@finai.com

Subject: Re: Demo issue - intermittent 503s at scale during coalescing test

Thanks for the signal, Alan. We pulled the runtime logs from the attached bundle and started a quick local repro. Preliminary notes:

- Observed 503s correlate with short-lived KV cache misses during batch merge. Sequence: merge start -> several concurrent requests try to read same KV page -> one path invalidates/refreshes while another assumes old state -> transient failure.
- This looks like a race in the in-memory cache invalidation path when two merged batches overlap on hot prefixes.

Immediate asks for FinAI so we can reproduce reliably:
1) sample request IDs for the failed requests (they show in your logs as req_id: 0x...)
2) SDK version (Camila requested this) and the exact coalescing flag you enabled (name/value)

Short-term mitigations we can push:
- Runtime patch (hotfix) to add a short lock around KV page refresh in the merge window (low risk, quick canary).
- SDK-side change to make coalescing conservative when KV cache TTLs are low (defensive).

Dev — I’m assigning you the initial investigation + stash for a hotfix PR. If we confirm a reproducible race I want an INF ticket and a canary plan.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Lead, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Demo issue - intermittent 503s at scale during coalescing test

Thanks — I pulled and annotated the logs (see runtime-logs-20261130.tar.gz attached). Quick summary of findings after 90m triage:

- Root cause (likely): race when merged batches overlap and KV cache invalidation re-populates the cache asynchronously. One request path sees a partially-initialized state and returns 503. Stack trace excerpt:
  - serving/runtime/kv_cache.cpp: line 218 (refresh_async)
  - serving/runtime/merge_manager.cpp: line 143 (apply_merge)

- Repro steps that worked locally: run 8 client threads with the SDK coalescing flag set to 0.8 (merge probability), set KV ttl to 2s, use overlapping prefixes (sample script attached in repro/).

Proposed immediate remediation:
1) Hotfix runtime: add minimal mutex around cache refresh in the merge window. I can get a PR ready by EOD.
2) SDK short-term workaround: expose an env var / flag that disables coalescing for now (less ideal but useful for procurement demos). Marissa — can your team ship that as a patch?

If we go hotfix -> canary -> roll, we should be able to restore confidence quickly. We’ll attach the failing req_ids to INF-9721.

Dev Patel
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime

On Tue, 01 Dec 2026 at 09:30 Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:

Subject: Re: Demo issue - intermittent 503s at scale during coalescing test

Thanks team — good catch. A couple notes from the SDK side:

- Coalescing in our SDK (released in v2.4) is opt-in and implemented client-side. We do fold requests if prefixes match and timing windows overlap. There’s no server-side contract that says merged requests are atomic — that's the gap.
- Immediate action: I opened PR #412 that adds a disable flag (REDWOOD_DISABLE_COALESCE=1) and a conservative fallback where the SDK will avoid merging when responses exceed a threshold length. Link: https://github.com/redwood/sdk/pull/412
- Longer term: we should add a compatibility mode where the SDK queries the server capability bit (supports-atomic-merge) and only coalesces when the runtime advertises safety. That’s a roadmap item but will take an engineering sprint.

For the procurement ask: I can cut a patch release (v2.4.1) with the env var in the next 24 hours if leadership signs off on the expedited path. Patch diff attached: sdk-disable-coalesce-patch.diff

Marissa Cole
Product, SDK Integrations
